candidate_analysis.explanation: The Random Forest assigns a 0.77 malware probability, and 19 of the top 20 n-grams push toward cryptojacking. Only TEST JNS (-0.007825) pushes toward benign. However, the evidence is weak for a high-confidence call. The SHAP contributions are small and evenly spread (about +0.005 to +0.013), with no dominant feature. Most of the top n-grams are generic stack and call-convention patterns: SUB PUSH, CALL PUSH, POP PUSH, ADD PUSH, PUSH CALL, MOV PUSH, POP MOV, POP CALL. These appear in nearly all compiled x86 code, so they are not specific to mining. The evidence lists no function names, API calls, or per-function locations, so none of these patterns can be tied to a mining routine. A few n-grams are potentially more interesting. MOV FLD and ADD FLD indicate x87 floating-point loads, and PXOR MOVDQA indicates SSE2 vector operations. Both could fit numeric or hash-style computation. POP XOR and SBB INC could fit bitwise or arithmetic mixing. But their frequencies are very low (ADD FLD 0.000026, PXOR MOVDQA 0.000041, SBB INC 0.000162), and floating-point and SSE code is also common in ordinary runtimes and libraries. The model leans malicious, but the contributions are diffuse, generic, and unsupported by any mining-specific evidence, so the result is suggestive but inconclusive.
